moat_against: Service contracts contestable at renewal; independents undercut OEM pricing
Pricing power limited — Q2 2026 maintenance pricing tempered for retention, margin down 180 bps
Technician labor shortage and wage/material inflation squeeze service margins
New Equipment cyclical and China-exposed — China NE sales down high-teens in Q2 2026, segment profit down 41%
KONE-TK Elevator combination creates a larger scaled service rival
Leveraged spin-off balance sheet — $6.86B net debt, negative book equity
moat_for: Largest global installed base (est. over 2.5M units) feeding recurring service revenue
Densest global technician network — response time decides service contracts
Safety regulation and downtime risk create real switching friction
Consolidated oligopoly with high entry barriers (approvals plus service infrastructure)
Aging installed base drives modernization — orders up 24%, backlog up 26% in Q2 2026
Proven through-cycle service profitability and installed-base pricing
moat_justification: The largest installed base in a regulated oligopoly converts into dense-network service economics and real switching friction, and service has held high margins through cycles; it stops short of wide because maintenance contracts are contestable at renewal by independents and rival OEMs, pricing power proved limited in 2026 (maintenance pricing tempered to protect retention), and New Equipment is a cyclical, China-exposed commodity contest.
name: OTIS WORLDWIDE CORPORATION
one_liner: High-quality service compounder, moat 7/10 — does not clear 15% at $69.76 (weighted IRR 9.0%, weighted IV@15 $35.99, hurdle-clearing price $35.99); even the super-bull case (13.6% IRR, $61.22 IV@15) stays below the hurdle.
